Developed by: BLACK HOLE STUDIO GOA Sachin Tendulkar or Vinod Kambli? Kapil Dev Offers Reality Check to Teenage Sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
 By Team Herald Published: 16 November 2026 Share SHARE Legendary former India captain Kapil Dev has weighed in on the growing buzz surrounding 15-year-old batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, urging the teenager to remain patient for opportunities in the national side while warning him against the perils of early fame, money, and off-field distractions.
 Sooryavanshi, who has quickly captivated cricket fans with his fearless, boundary-hitting style, featured in only two matches during India’s recent five-match T20I series against New Zealand. With established openers Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson occupying the top spots, the youngster has had to bide his time on the sidelines—a situation that has sparked considerable debate among fans and pundits alike.

 Speaking during an interaction with Mid-Day , Kapil acknowledged the excitement surrounding the teenager’s explosive batting, noting that fans of all ages love watching a youngster clear the ropes. However, the 1983 World Cup-winning captain stressed that raw talent alone is not enough at the international level and that Sooryavanshi still has a long journey ahead.
 “He still has a long way to go. Though he’s part of the Indian team, he doesn’t get enough chances… He needs more time. There is no shortage of talent,” Kapil observed, advising the youngster to keep his focus strictly on the game rather than getting swept up by financial rewards or public attention.
 To illustrate the critical crossroads facing young prodigies, Kapil drew a poignant comparison between two of Indian cricket’s most famous teenage sensations from the late 1980s: Sachin Tendulkar and Vinod Kambli.
 “At the age of 15, he has only cricket [to think about]. When he reaches 18 or 19, other things will emerge—parties and other distractions. Will he be like Sachin Tendulkar or Vinod Kambli? It’s very difficult to say at this stage,” Kapil remarked.
 - Advertisement - The contrast between Tendulkar and Kambli serves as a classic cautionary tale in Indian sports. While both burst onto the scene with immense promise—and many initially considered Kambli the more naturally gifted batter—their trajectories diverged dramatically. Tendulkar’s unmatched discipline propelled him to become the highest run-scorer in both Test and ODI history, whereas Kambli’s international career faded prematurely, largely derailed by a glamorous lifestyle and a lack of off-field focus.
